rules: The satp CSR is an SXLEN-bit read/write register.
The satp register contains PPN, ASID, and MODE fields.
The satp.PPN field holds the physical page number of the root page table, which is the supervisor physical address divided by 4 KiB.
The satp.ASID field holds an address space identifier to facilitate address-translation fences on a per-addressspace basis.
The satp.MODE field selects the current address-translation scheme.
When SXLEN=32, the satp encodings corresponding to MODE=Bare and ASID[8:7]=3 are designated for custom use.
When SXLEN=32, the satp encodings corresponding to MODE=Bare and ASID[8:7]≠3 are reserved for future standard use.
When SXLEN=64, all satp encodings corresponding to MODE=Bare are reserved for future standard use.
When the satp.MODE field is set to Bare, supervisor virtual addresses are equal to supervisor physical addresses.
When the satp.MODE field is set to Bare, there is no additional memory protection beyond the physical memory protection scheme.
To select MODE=Bare when SXLEN=32, software must write zero to the remaining fields of satp (bits 30-0).
To select MODE=Bare when SXLEN=64, software must write zero to the remaining fields of satp (bits 59-0).
When SXLEN=32, the only valid setting for the satp.MODE field other than Bare is Sv32.
When SXLEN=64, the valid settings for the satp.MODE field are Sv39, Sv48, and Sv57.
If satp is written with an unsupported MODE, the entire write has no effect and no fields in satp are modified.
The number of ASID bits in the satp.ASID field is UNSPECIFIED.
The number of implemented ASID bits (ASIDLEN) is determined by writing a one to every bit position in the ASID field and reading back the value in satp.
If ASIDLEN is greater than 0, the bits ASID[ASIDLEN-1:0] in the satp register are writable.
The maximal value of ASIDLEN is 9 for Sv32 and 16 for Sv39, Sv48, and Sv57.
The satp CSR is considered active when the effective privilege mode is S-mode or U-mode.
The address-translation algorithm may only begin using a given value of satp when satp is active.
Writing satp does not imply any ordering constraints between page-table updates and subsequent address translations.
Writing satp does not imply any invalidation of address-translation caches.
